items.title: You Can Now Try Apple's Unreleased Copland OS in Your Browser
items.snippet: In the mid–1990s, Apple worked on an operating system called Copland, which was announced but never commercially released because of project management issues and feature creep. Parts of Copland were eventually included in Mac OS 7.6 and Mac OS 8, but it was so problematic as a whole that Apple nixed it before it was finished. Michael Steil, who works to reverse engineer vintage hardware and software, was recently able to get Copland running in emulation. items.snippet: Macworld iOS 27 has finally delivered on the new Siri promise Apple made back in 2024, but many people who were persuaded to buy an iPhone 16 at the time by ads touting the feature still feel cheated that it took so long. items.title: Microsoft brings Snapdragon X2 Plus to 13-inch Surface Laptop, 12-inch Surface Pro
items.snippet: Microsoft's lowest-end systems are getting upgrades to Qualcomm's latest Snapdragon X2 Plus processors.

items.title: Alibaba claims new Qwen Image 2.1 AI model beats Google Nano Banana 2.0 with minuscule 7B parameter model
items.snippet: Alibaba Group's AI division has released Qwen 2.1 Image, an ultra-lightweight image generation model with just 7B parameters, able to run on local hardware like the RTX 3090.

items.title: $14,000 gaming PC features 70 handcrafted titanium cherry blossoms which unfurl as temperatures rise
items.snippet: The Aftershock PC Cherry Bloom includes 70 hand-crafted cherry blossoms made of titanium alloy that open and close with the heat generated by the PC.

items.title: Sony INZONE M10S II 27-inch 540 Hz QHD OLED gaming monitor review: A major player in a crowded field
items.snippet: Sony brings saturated color and speedy gameplay to the OLED genre with its INZONE M10S II 27-inch QHD monitor. It boasts a 540 Hz refresh rate, 720 Hz at HD resolution, Adaptive-Sync, HDR, and wide-gamut color.

items.title: China's ByteDance gained access to over 2,000 Nvidia B200 chips through Norway data center
items.snippet: UK-based Nscale signed a deal with Spring (SG) Pte Ltd, which is a subsidiary of Chinese tech giant ByteDance. The company did not make any direct mention of the TikTok parent in its filings for a U.S. IPO, while a supporting document only labeled Spring as a significant customer.

items.title: Alibaba unveils Zhenwu V900 AI accelerator, claims it's 'the most powerful AI chip in China'
items.snippet: Alibaba’s T-Head Zhenwu V900 claims three times the M890’s performance with 216GB of memory as Alibaba targets 10T-parameter Qwen

items.title: Upgrade your gaming experience with this 27-inch Acer 1440p 270Hz panel that’s an incredible 45% off
items.snippet: Jump into high-refresh-rate 1440p gaming without breaking the bank: Acer's 27-inch 1440p 270Hz IPS gaming monitor is just $179, a whopping 45% off

items.title: AMD begins to add GDDR7 support to its Linux GPU drivers
items.snippet: Recent changes to AMD's Linux drivers to enable GDDR7 memory and other graphics IP blocks could indicate that that enablement work on its RDNA 5 GPUs is under way.

items.title: This 32GB Corsair Vengeance DDR5-6000 memory is the cheapest kit available
items.snippet: Get a great deal on 32GB Corsair Vengeance DDR5-6000 RAM. Just $439 after promo code SSF73844 yields one of the lowest priced 32GB kits available today

items.title: Durabook Z14I-DX3 rugged mobile workstation folds three screens into a 9.8 kg chassis
items.snippet: Built for military, emergency services and industrial applications, the Z14I-DX3 packs three sunlight-readable 14-inch touchscreens and up to RTX 5000 Ada graphics into one exceptionally rugged mobile workstation.

items.title: Get this spiffy, stealthy MSI Gaming Trio RTX 5090 for just $4,299
items.snippet: Walmart has MSI's GeForce RTX 5090 Gaming Trio for just $4299 as part of its GeForce Week event, a rare deal on the most powerful graphics card around as the AI boom drives prices ever higher.

items.title: ‘We’ll be the first to mine Bitcoin in space’ says Nvidia-backed startup
items.snippet: An Nvidia-backed startup plans to establish a Bitcoin mining operation in space before the year is out.

items.title: Gaming PC with RTX 5060, 32GB of RAM, and 1TB of storage gets $500 discount
items.snippet: Newegg's ABS Cyclone Aqua prebuilt combines Intel's 20-core Core i7-14700F with Nvidia's RTX 5060 8GB, and 32GB of DDR4 memory for less than the cost of building a comparable system

items.title: Memory chips are now more expensive than compute chips on a per-area basis
items.snippet: DRAM makers may potentially get more money for their wafers than TSMC gets for its N3 wafers.

items.title: Raspberry Pi locks boards to factory RAM capacities in firmware
items.snippet: Raspberry Pi users are being firmware blocked from swapping the RAM chips on their SBCs for repairs or upgrades.

items.title: This $299 2TB MSI SSD is one of the least expensive PCIe 4.0 SSDs you can buy right now
items.snippet: Get a solid deal on the 2TB MSI Spatium M461 SSD. Just $299 after promo code nets one of the least expensive Gen 4x4 SSDs available today.

items.title: New DapuStor SSD pairs high-capacity QLC with a permanent pSLC region
items.snippet: DapuStor’s dual-mode J5060 QLC SSD runs part of its NAND as pSLC, trading 4TB of a 30.72TB drive for 800GB of fast flash.

items.title: China's CXMT hits 12nm-class DRAM milestone
items.snippet: China's DRAM champion CXMT has begun mass production using its 5th Geb DRAM process technology

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic scramble for smaller data centers as massive gigawatt projects lag
items.snippet: OpenAI and Anthropic are seeking to secure immediate capacity, through smaller data center deals, to meet current demand, despite spending billions on massive deals elsewhere.

items.title: Get the world’s fastest gaming CPU and a DLSS 5-capable GPU in a gaming PC for $2,299
items.snippet: Walmart is selling a CyberPowerPC gaming PC with a Ryzen 7 9800X3D, GeForce RTX 5080 Founders Edition, 32GB of DDR5-6000 memory, and a 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD for $2,299.

items.title: AMD beats Intel to the trillion-dollar club as stock price soars
items.snippet: AMD has crossed the $1 trillion market cap mark, joining an exclusive list of less than two dozen companies around the world.

items.title: AMD Ryzen 5 5500F and 7500 show up at retail with pricing above MSRP
items.snippet: Nearly two weeks after they were announced, AMD's Ryzen 5 5500F and 7500 (non-F) are available for sale, though prices are slightly above MSRP.

items.title: New RTX 5070 Autumn Limited Edition gaming GPU doubles as an air freshener with built-in 'e-sports aromatherapy'
items.snippet: AX Gaming has revealed its latest seasonal anime-themed limited edition graphics card which, this time, is designed to please your nose as much as your eyes.

items.title: Snag the least expensive 32GB DDR5-6000 memory kit available for only $429
items.snippet: Buy 32GB of V-Color Manta XSky RAM for only $429. This capable, white DDR5-6000 CL30 kit is one of the best deals out for the speed and timings

items.title: TypeSafe AI's Jev offers an alternative to LLMs that claims to be 193x faster and 445x cheaper
items.snippet: Last week saw the debut of TypeSafe AI's Jev, its first "System One" model. Rather than chatting with users like conventional LLMs, it's strictly designed for statement evaluation and decision-making, for programming purposes.

items.title: Hands-on with Googlebooks — Five models, the new Googlebook OS, and a Mac-style experience for Android users at premium prices
items.snippet: Google has detailed its new Googlebooks, five laptops combining Android and ChromeOS to make a Mac-like experience for Android users, with a ton of Gemini tacked on.

items.title: PlayStation 3 emulation devs work around an Nvidia bug for up to 37% faster performance
items.snippet: The developers of RPCS3 have found a workaround for an Nvidia driver bug and are touting up to 37% performance gains.

items.title: Cloudflare saves 100 TB of RAM again, this time by slashing server hashes by 90%

items.title: Specops Device Trust: Device-based access control beyond MFA
items.snippet: Specops Device Trust is a cloud-based security product from Specops Software (part of Outpost24) that ties access decisions to user identity and the device's security state. It addresses a specific gap that multi-factor authentication (MFA) alone cannot close: an attacker who steals a session token or login credentials can still access your systems if access decisions are based solely on user identity. The product binds users to enrolled, verified devices and continuously checks device security throughout every session. This article covers how Specops Device Trust works, what it checks, and how to deploy it. Source

items.title: F5 fixes actively exploited zero-day flaw in BIG-IP APM
items.snippet: Technology company F5 fixed a critical remote code execution vulnerability in its BIG-IP Access Policy Manager (APM) platform on Tuesday. The flaw impacts deployments configured as OAuth authorization servers and was already under active exploitation in the wild before the patch became available. BIG-IP APM is a software component in F5’s BIG-IP hardware platform that enables companies to control access to internal network resources. APM performs various client-side checks and handles authorization and authentication, along with providing VPN connectivity for remote users.
